beats.text: Five books that will quietly sharpen the way you think.
One. Plato's Republic — watch Socrates take an idea apart until only the truth is left.
Two. Meditations — Marcus Aurelius on seeing things as they are, stripped of your stories.
Three. Montaigne's Essays — the art of questioning your own certainties, honestly.
Four. Bacon's essays — short, sharp lessons in judging evidence over habit.
Five. Letters from a Stoic — Seneca turning philosophy into practical, everyday clear thinking.
Reading great minds is how you learn to argue with your own. Explainers are on the channel.
